qa_results.question: Tell me about the driving experience
qa_results.answer: The Hyundai Creta offers a smooth and refined driving experience, especially with the 1.5-liter naturally aspirated petrol engine. It is best suited for city driving with ample acceleration for relaxed driving. The automatic (CVT) model provides a jerk-free drive, making it very calming. It cruises effortlessly at speeds of 100-120kmph. However, overtakes will need planning at higher speeds, especially if you're traveling with family and/or luggage. The 1.5-liter turbo-petrol engine offers an exciting drive, suitable for those who want to drive themselves, mostly on the highway. It drives smoothly in heavy traffic and overtakes in the city are easy. The dual clutch automatic transmission (DCT) feels smooth when driving in a relaxed manner and quick and snappy when needed. Hitting triple-digit speeds is easy and even overtaking at those higher speeds doesn't take much effort. However, it's not very efficient in the city with 10kmpl being the best case scenario in heavy traffic. The 1.5-liter diesel engine is amongst the smoothest in the market with above-average refinement levels. It offers an effortless drive in the city while the performance is adequate for highway usage. With plenty of low-end torque, you don't need to downshift frequently with the manual. The automatic version offers smooth shifts, even if it is slightly slow to respond, especially compared to the DCT. The diesel-automatic combination would be my pick out of all options since it offers the best balance of performance and fuel economy. The Creta's suspension absorbs most of the city's rough roads and potholes, while maintaining stability and comfort over undulations or expansion joints on the highway. However, a constant up/down movement can be felt inside if the road surface isn't smooth, which can cause slight discomfort on longer highway trips. It also poses strong braking performance with a 100-0kmph stopping distance of 38.12 meters.
